name: moreutils
desc: Collection of tools that nobody wrote when UNIX was young
why: A collection of forgotten Unix tools like sponge and ifdata; widely installed but the odd corners still reward exploring.

brief.what_it_is: moreutils is a collection of small general-purpose Unix command-line tools, fifteen in all: chronic, combine, errno, ifdata, ifne, isutf8, lckdo, mispipe, parallel, pee, sponge, ts, vidir, vipe, and zrun. Each takes ordinary text or arguments from the shell and does one narrow job, such as soaking up stdin into a file, timestamping lines, or opening a directory listing in your editor for renaming. The page describes them as the basic tools that were never written. The tools are installed as separate executables, so they slot into existing pipelines.
brief.why_it_exists: The author's view is that the most basic tools fall through the cracks and are never noticed by people who could benefit from them, so the collection was born to stop these programs from falling through the cracks.

commands_seen.context: Page's example of sponge, which it calls probably the most general-purpose tool in the collection: sponge reads all of stdin before writing, so the pipeline can safely rewrite /etc/passwd in place.
Example usage for a tmp tool that is only proposed under 'Tools under consideration' and is not among the shipped executables; it would stash stdin in a temp file and pass it to the named program.

brief.install_notes: Packaged as a Debian package and available via apt; the page says it is also in Ubuntu and, per the author, several other Linux distributions. The source tarball is on packages.debian.org. The git repository can be cloned from git://git.joeyh.name/moreutils. The page gives no build steps, runtime, or configuration beyond that. The brew caveats field was empty.
brief.standout: Rather than a single clever tool, it is a deliberate curation project: the author blogged about a missing general-purpose Unix tool, took feedback, and concluded that the basics were simply overlooked. The page also keeps a visible list of rejected and under-consideration tools with reasons, such as add and todist being moved to numutils and srename duplicating Perl's rename.
brief.status: Maintained by one author, Joey Hess, though the page is not dated and shows no release dates or commit dates. The latest listed news item is version 0.70, which covers a vidir padding fix, zstd support in zrun, and a ts change closing a Debian bug. The page also says the collection is closed to new tools and invites someone to take over editorial responsibility and maintenance. Recency beyond that is unknown.
brief.caveats: The page says the collection is closed to suggestions for new tools, and it asks for a new maintainer. Several tools are ideas only, such as connect, tmp, cattail, and phoenix, and the TODO notes that pee cannot yet do non-blocking I/O. The page gives no platform, licence, or build information. The 0.69 news entry is a jab at pkgx.dev in the Makefile, so the project is opinionated about packaging.
quotes: moreutils is a collection of the unix tools that nobody thought to write long ago when unix was young.
And so the moreutils collection was born, to stop these programs from falling through the cracks.
This collection is closed at this time for suggestions of additional tools to add to it.
